Record a self-signal

Source: R/core-signal-record.R
hr_signal.Rd

hr_signal() writes a value the package produced about its own work into a run's trace, and hr_signals() reads every recorded signal back as one table. Recording is all that happens: no signal changes what a reader does unless a calibration record and a passing threshold allow it (see hr_calibrate_signal(), hr_gate_threshold() and hr_apply_signal()).

Usage

hr_signal(name, value, trace = NULL, item_id = NA_character_, refs = NULL)

hr_signals(x, name = NULL)

Arguments

name

For hr_signal(), the signal's name, one string, such as "gr.iterative.can_answer". For hr_signals(), the names to keep, or NULL (the default) for every signal.

value

The value: a logical, numeric or character vector with at least one element and no NA for a logical or numeric one. Several values record several observations of the signal in one step.

trace

A gr_trace to record into, or an object holding one in $trace (an answer). NULL records nothing and only returns the signal.

item_id

The item each value is about: one value, or one per element of value. NA when the caller has no item id.

refs

NULL, or a named list of references (a round, a section number), each element either one value or one per element of value.

x

For hr_signals(): a gr_trace, an object holding one in $trace (an answer, a stage result), or a list of these, such as the answers of several runs.

Value

hr_signal() returns an hr_signal invisibly: a list with name, value, type ("logical", "numeric" or "character"), item_id, refs and step (the step number in the trace, or NA).

hr_signals() returns a data frame with one row per recorded value: run_id, step, source and recipe (the document and recipe the step was stamped with, or NA), signal, type, item_id, index (the value's position within its step), value (as text), score (the value as a number: 1 or 0 for a logical, the number for a numeric, NA for text) and refs (the references for that value as a JSON object, or NA). A trace reached more than once in x (the same trace object, as the answers of one comparison share it) lists each step once; two separate traces are both read, even with the same run_id.

Details

A signal is stored as a local step labelled "signal", with the name, value, item and references in its detail. A local step is not a request, so it is not a row of as.data.frame(trace), is not counted in trace$calls, and changes no request or cache key.

Three signals are recorded by the readers:

gr.iterative.can_answer

One per step of the iterative reader whose reply parsed: TRUE when the step said it could answer. refs$round is the round.

gr.preview.skip

One value per section after the preview reader's plan: TRUE for a section the plan marked skip. refs$section is the section number and refs$treatment what the plan said.

gr.ensemble.adjudicate

How the ensemble reader settled its members: "model" when the adjudication request answered, "concatenated" when it failed and the findings were joined, or "single member" when only one member answered.

See also

hr_calibrate_signal(), hr_signal_policy()

Other signals: hr_calibrate_signal(), hr_calibration_valid(), hr_gate_threshold(), hr_signal_policy()

Examples

tr <- gr_trace()
hr_signal("demo.confident", TRUE, tr, item_id = "q1")
hr_signal("demo.confident", c(0.9, 0.2), tr, item_id = c("q2", "q3"))
hr_signals(tr)
#>                          run_id step source recipe         signal    type
#> 1 run_20261110015437.595_6128b4    1   <NA>   <NA> demo.confident logical
#> 2 run_20261110015437.595_6128b4    2   <NA>   <NA> demo.confident numeric
#> 3 run_20261110015437.595_6128b4    2   <NA>   <NA> demo.confident numeric
#>   item_id index value score refs
#> 1      q1     1  TRUE   1.0 <NA>
#> 2      q2     1   0.9   0.9 <NA>
#> 3      q3     2   0.2   0.2 <NA>

# The readers record their own signals.
cl <- gr_mock_client(function(m, p) {
  '{"can_answer": true, "answer": "45.2 million dollars", "next_query": ""}'
})
ch <- gr_segment(gr_example(), list(method = "sentence", max_tokens = 150))
#> Using cached ingestion for this document + settings.
#> Segmenting with 'sentence' (cap 150 tokens, overlap 0).
ans <- gr_read(ch, "What was revenue?", cl, "iterative")
#> Reading with 'iterative' (topk|rounds*2|forward) over 5 chunk(s).
hr_signals(ans)
#>                          run_id step source recipe                  signal
#> 1 run_20261110015437.647_3ba1a1    5   <NA>   <NA> gr.iterative.can_answer
#>      type item_id index value score        refs
#> 1 logical    <NA>     1  TRUE     1 {"round":1}
